chapter_name: Chapter 03: Gap Filling and Sentence Conjunctions
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master sentence cohesion using various conjunctions and apply grammatical rules (agreement, tense, vocabulary) to accurately complete cloze passages.]
warm_up_hook: 🌉 Have you ever tried crossing a broken bridge? Conjunctions are the planks that connect disconnected ideas, and gap-filling is the art of choosing the perfectly sized plank so your reader doesn't fall through! Let's bridge the gap! 🧩

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So) join equal parts of a sentence. Correlative conjunctions come in pairs (either/or, neither/nor, not only/but also) to balance sentence structures.
examples_or_templates: Coordinating: The movie was long, but it was highly entertaining.
Correlative: She is not only brilliant but also incredibly humble.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Subordinating conjunctions (although, since, unless, whereas) link a dependent clause to an independent one. They establish relationships like contrast, cause-and-effect, or time, creating flow in complex writing.
examples_or_templates: Contrast: Whereas John loves sports, his brother prefers reading.
Condition: We will not reach on time unless we take a taxi.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: To solve gap fills, read the whole passage first for context. Look at the words immediately before and after the blank. Determine the part of speech required (noun, verb, preposition, conjunction) and check subject-verb agreement and tense.
examples_or_templates: Sentence: Despite the heavy rain, they _____ to reach the summit.
Analysis: We need a past tense verb showing success. Answer: 'managed'.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Choose the correct conjunction: '_____ he was feeling unwell, he decided to attend the crucial meeting.'
❓ Fill in the gap: 'Neither the manager nor the employees _____ aware of the new policy.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Join these two sentences using a correlative conjunction: 'He cannot read. He cannot write.'
subjective_practice.hint: Use the pair that indicates two negative options (neither... nor).

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank logically: 'She studied diligently for months; __________, she scored the highest in the district.'
subjective_practice.hint: You need a conjunctive adverb that shows a result or conclusion (e.g., consequently, therefore).

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Identify the clue to fill the gap: 'The migration of birds is a fascinating phenomenon _____ has puzzled scientists for centuries.'
subjective_practice.hint: The blank requires a relative pronoun that refers back to 'phenomenon'.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🧩 The Missing Link Challenge
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write a 5-sentence paragraph about a recent event or a movie you watched. Remove 5 connecting words (conjunctions or prepositions) and replace them with blanks. Swap your paragraph with a partner and see if they can fill in the exact gaps!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Coordinating and Correlative conjunctions balance sentences and join ideas of equal importance.
⭐ Subordinating conjunctions create dependent clauses that add nuance like reason, time, or contrast.
⭐ Successful gap filling requires analyzing context, parts of speech, and grammatical rules before choosing a word.
